newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher led by Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher led by Wall Street.

text.p: Israeli shares closed broadly higher on Tuesday following the rise of Israeli shares traded on Nasdaq and boosted by falling bond yields, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 1.56 percent, or 4.05 points, to 263.77 on an all-share turnover of 138 million shekels against 118 million shekels on Thursday, which had been the last day of trading before the long Israeli Independence Day weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.35 percent higher at 272.10.
"The market looks very good and investors are optimistic. The recent rise of Israeli shares traded in New York adds to the positive mood," said Ronen Kaufman of Nesuah Trading and Investments.

Zvi Hoffman of Meitav Investments and Securities added that investors gained confidence from falling yields on long CPI-linked bonds. "Declining yields are a very positive sign for the market. This, together with the rise of Israeli shares on Wall Street, helped the market rise today," he said.

"One of the main reasons for the positive mood is that there are not many sellers and the market is rising sharply on moderate volume. The fact that foreign investors were also very active buying today adds to the optimism," Kaufman added.
Nice Systems Ltd surged 9.0 percent to 9,023 agorot. Traders said Nice's Tel Aviv stock price had not yet closed the arbitrage gap with its Nasdaq-traded share.

In addition, Lehman Brothers raised its 1997 earnings estimate for Nice citing a strong first quarter. Nice earned $0.28 a share in the first quarter against a consensus estimate of $0.26. Lehman upgraded Nice's earnings per share estimate for all of 1997 to $1.29 from $1.26.

The most active shares were Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which rose 2.75 percent to 19,468 agorot on turnover of 9.7 million shekels; Israel Chemicals, which fell 0.25 percent to 395 on volume of 7.1 million shekels; and Bank Hapoalim, which gained 2.0 percent to 718 agorot on volume of 5.9 million shekels.
